title: 3.4.17 Lab: Fix a Broken Arrow
description: A two-parameter arrow function was written without the parentheses around its parameters, so the line will not parse. Fix it. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Run the broken code
steps.instructions: Run the starter. The line where the arrow is defined throws a syntax error before anything else runs. The message may not mention parentheses; the clue is that the error is on the line that defines the arrow.

steps.title: Find what is missing
steps.instructions: The arrow has two parameters but no parentheses around them. Parentheses are optional for exactly one parameter — they become required the moment a second one appears.

steps.title: Fix the parameter list and run it
steps.instructions: Put parentheses around the two parameters, leaving the arrow body unchanged. Run it and confirm the call prints the product of the two arguments.

requirements.title: Parameters wrapped in parentheses
requirements.description: An arrow function is written with parentheses around its parameter list. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Look at the left of the arrow. A parameter list with more than one name has to be wrapped in a pair of parentheses.

requirements.title: Two parameters inside the parentheses
requirements.description: The parenthesised parameter list holds two comma-separated parameters. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Both names, separated by a comma, go inside the one pair of parentheses before =>.

requirements.title: The fixed code runs and prints
requirements.description: Once the arrow parses, the console.log line runs and prints a result. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: A syntax error stops the whole file, so nothing prints until the parameter list is fixed. Fix it and press Run.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed. Fix the arrow so the file runs, and keep the console.log line.

requirements.title: area is an arrow with two parameters
requirements.description: area itself is a const holding an arrow with two parameters in parentheses. Help: 3.4.8 (The Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Fix the arrow that is there: const area = (w, h) => w * h; Do not swap it for a function declaration.

requirements.title: area returns the product of its two arguments
requirements.description: area(3, 4) is 12 and area(5, 6) is 30. Help: 3.4.8 (Shorthand Rules)
requirements.hint: Only the parameter list is broken. Wrap both parameters in parentheses and leave the body (w * h) exactly as it is.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "3.4.17 Lab: Fix a Broken Arrow". The task they were given: Run the starter. The line where the arrow is defined throws a syntax error before anything else runs. The message may not mention parentheses; the clue is that the error is on the line that defines the arrow. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
